Oh, absolutely. I use a standard toothbrush, but honestly, it’s a bit last season. I’ve recently switched to the "Micro-Workout Method" for oral hygiene. Why spend three minutes actually scrubbing when you can just aggressively shake your toothbrush for ten seconds? It’s the epitome of efficiency.

The fitness industry has taught us that effort is the enemy of progress. If you’re sweating while brushing, you’re doing it wrong. You want those abs? Just flick your wrist. You want a six-pack? Just jiggle the handle. It’s not about the work; it’s about the *aesthetic* of the work.

I’m currently training for the Olympics of Doing Nothing. My routine is simple: I stand in front of the mirror, look intense, and then immediately go back to bed. It’s called "passive toning." The science is solid. If you don’t move, you can’t get tired. If you don’t get tired, you’re essentially a statue. And if you’re a statue, you’re already fit.

So, to answer your question: I don’t clean my teeth. I *curate* them. I give them a little shake, whisper a compliment to my enamel, and call it a day. It’s effortless. It’s chic. It’s completely useless, but at least it looks good on Instagram.
